title: Privacy Policy
contentHtml:
Privacy Policy

Platform: learn.cogniumlabs.io

Effective Date: 20 May 2026

Last Updated: 20 May 2026

1. Introduction

Cognium Labs (OPC) Private Limited (the "Company", "We", "Us" or "Our") respects Your privacy and is committed to protecting Your Personal Data. This Privacy Policy ("Policy") describes how We collect, use, store, process, share, disclose and otherwise handle Your Personal Data when You access or use Our website learn.cogniumlabs.io, mobile applications, or any related products, courses, classes, study material, doubt-resolution tools, assessments, mentorship and other educational services (collectively, the "Services").

This Policy is published in accordance with: (a) the Information Technology Act, 2000 ("IT Act") and the Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011 ("SPDI Rules"); (b) the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 ("IT Rules, 2021") and the rules made thereunder, as amended from time to time.

By accessing or using the Services, or by providing Your Personal Data to Us, You confirm that You have read and understood this Policy and consent to the collection, use, processing, storage, sharing and disclosure of Your Personal Data in accordance with this Policy. If You do not agree to this Policy, please do not use the Services.

2. Definitions

  • "Data Fiduciary" means any person who, alone or in conjunction with other persons, determines the purpose and means of processing of Personal Data. For the Services, the Data Fiduciary is the Company.
  • "Data Principal" means the individual to whom the Personal Data relates and, where such individual is a Child, includes the parents or lawful guardian of such Child, and where such individual is a person with disability, includes her lawful guardian acting on her behalf.
  • "Personal Data" means any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data.
  • "Processing", in relation to Personal Data, means any operation or set of operations performed on Personal Data, including collection, recording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation, retrieval, use, alignment or combination, indexing, sharing, disclosure by transmission, dissemination, restriction, erasure or destruction.
  • "Child" / "Minor" means an individual who has not completed the age of 18 (eighteen) years.

3. Scope and Applicability

3.1 This Policy applies to the processing of digital Personal Data within the territory of India, including Personal Data collected online and Personal Data collected offline that is subsequently digitised. This Policy also applies to processing of Personal Data outside India where such processing is in connection with offering goods or services to Data Principals within India.

3.2 This Policy does not apply to (a) Personal Data processed by an individual for purely personal or domestic purposes; or (b) Personal Data made publicly available by the Data Principal herself or by any other person under a legal obligation to make such Personal Data publicly available.

3.3 The Platform may contain links to third-party websites and services. This Policy does not apply to information collected by such third parties. Please review the privacy policies of such third parties before sharing Your Personal Data.

4. Information We Collect

4.1 Information You provide directly to Us

When You register, subscribe or otherwise interact with the Services, We may collect the following categories of Personal Data:

  • Identification & contact details: full name, date of birth / age, gender, school / college, class or grade, board, residential address, city, state, PIN code, email address, mobile number.
  • Account credentials: username, password (stored in hashed/encrypted form), security questions and answers.
  • Parent / Guardian details (for Minors): name, relationship, email, mobile number, address and proof of identity / age as required for verifiable consent.
  • Educational interests & preferences: target examination, subjects, course preferences, study schedule, learning goals.
  • Payment information: billing name and address, GSTIN (if any), payment-instrument tokens, transaction reference numbers, invoices. Full payment card numbers are processed only by RBI-authorised payment aggregators / payment gateways and are not stored by Us in plaintext form.
  • Identity / KYC documents (where required): Aadhaar (only as permitted under law and in masked/tokenised form), PAN, photograph, school identity card or other government-issued identity proof.
  • Health-related information (where relevant): learning-disability disclosures, accessibility requirements or medical conditions voluntarily shared by You to enable accommodations.
  • Communications: correspondence with Our customer support, complaints, feedback, survey responses.
  • User Generated Content: doubts, questions, answers, assignments, mock tests, project submissions, recordings of voice/video during live classes, ratings and reviews.

4.2 Information collected automatically

When You access the Services, We automatically collect technical and usage information, including:

  • Device information: device model, operating system and version, unique device identifiers, mobile network information, IP address, browser type, language settings.
  • Usage data: pages visited, features used, time spent, lessons watched, tests attempted, scores, clickstream, navigation paths, referrer URLs.
  • Location data: approximate location derived from IP address. Precise GPS location is collected only with Your explicit permission and only when required by a specific feature (for example, finding a nearby learning centre).
  • Camera / microphone / screen data: with Your prior permission, We may access Your camera, microphone and screen for live classes, doubt-resolution sessions, mock interviews and remote proctoring. Such recordings are used solely for the educational purpose disclosed at the time of capture.
  • Cookies and similar technologies: see Clause 13 below.

4.3 Information from third parties

We may receive Personal Data about You from third parties such as: (a) social media platforms when You sign in using Your Google, Apple or other third-party account; (b) referral partners; (c) educational institutions or coaching partners with whom You are associated; (d) payment service providers; (e) public sources; and (f) governmental authorities, in each case in compliance with Applicable Law.

5. Legal Basis for Processing

We process Personal Data on the following grounds:

  • Consent. Personal Data is processed primarily on the basis of Your free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous consent indicated by a clear affirmative action. Consent is sought through this Policy and the consent notice presented at the point of collection.
  • Certain Legitimate Uses including: (a) where You have voluntarily provided Personal Data for a specified purpose; (b) for the performance of any function under any law; (c) for compliance with any judgment, decree or order; (d) for responding to a medical emergency; (e) for ensuring safety or providing assistance during a disaster or breakdown of public order; and (f) for the purposes of employment.

6. Purposes of Processing

We process Your Personal Data for the following purposes:

  • to provide, deliver, personalise, maintain, improve and develop the Services (including live classes, recorded lectures, doubt resolution, assessments, reports and study material);
  • to create and manage Your Account, verify Your identity, and authenticate Your access to the Services;
  • to process payments, generate invoices, manage Subscriptions, send receipts and perform related financial and accounting functions;
  • to communicate with You regarding the Services, including service-related announcements, updates, technical notices, security alerts and administrative messages;
  • to provide personalised learning experiences, recommend content, generate performance analytics and progress reports;
  • to provide customer support, respond to queries, resolve disputes and enforce Our Terms of Service and other policies;
  • to detect, prevent, mitigate and investigate fraud, abuse, unauthorised access, intellectual property violations and other malicious activities;
  • to send promotional and marketing communications regarding Our Services and products (where You have consented or such communications are otherwise permitted by Applicable Law). You may opt out of such communications at any time;
  • to conduct research, analytics, demographic studies and surveys to improve the Services. Where feasible, such activities are conducted on anonymised or aggregated data;
  • to comply with Applicable Law, legal process, government and regulatory requests, and to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

7. Consent, Notice and Withdrawal

7.1 This Policy, together with the consent notice presented to You at the time of collection, constitutes the notice describing: (a) the items of Personal Data being processed; (b) the specific purpose for which it is being processed; (c) the manner in which You may exercise Your rights.

7.2 Withdrawal of Consent. You have the right to withdraw Your consent at any time. Withdrawal of consent will be as easy as giving consent. You may withdraw consent through (a) Your Account settings on the Platform; or (b) a written request at support@cogniumlabs.io.

7.3 The consequences of withdrawal shall be borne by You. Where withdrawal of consent makes it impossible for Us to continue providing certain Services, We may be unable to provide such Services. The lawfulness of processing carried out on the basis of consent before its withdrawal shall remain unaffected, and We may continue processing data where another lawful ground (such as a legitimate use or legal obligation) applies.

8. Sharing and Disclosure of Personal Data

8.1 We do not sell Your Personal Data. We share Personal Data only as described below and only to the extent reasonably necessary:

  • Service providers / Data Processors: with vetted third-party Data Processors who act on Our behalf. These include cloud hosting, content delivery, analytics, email/SMS dispatch, payment processing, customer support, KYC/identity verification, anti-fraud, and communications providers.
  • Educational and content partners: faculty, instructors, mentors, examination bodies, school / coaching partners and content publishers, strictly to deliver the Services or assessments You have requested.
  • Legal & regulatory disclosures: with courts, tribunals, regulators, law enforcement and other governmental authorities when required by a binding order, summons, subpoena or under Applicable Law.
  • Business transfers: in connection with a merger, acquisition, financing, reorganisation, bankruptcy, receivership or sale of all or part of Our business or assets, subject to confidentiality and Applicable Law.
  • Group entities and affiliates: with Our holding company, subsidiaries and affiliates for purposes consistent with this Policy.
  • With Your consent: with any other party where You have provided specific consent for such disclosure.

8.2 We require all third-party recipients to (i) process Personal Data only for the purposes for which it was shared; (ii) implement reasonable security safeguards; and (iii) comply with all Applicable Laws relating to data protection.

8.3 Organisation context. Where You belong to an organisation on the Platform (a school, college, coaching centre or employer) and choose to act in that organisation's context, the content You create there — including decks, study material, assessments and the documents You upload — is stored in that organisation's library rather than Your personal one, and is accessible to that organisation's administrators and delegates. Content You create in Your personal profile is not visible to them. Which of the two You are working in is shown in the application and is Your choice at the time; where an action offers a choice of destination, the destination You select determines who can see the result. The organisation is responsible under the Terms of Service for the lawfulness of the material it directs or permits its members to upload.

9. Cross-Border Data Transfers

9.1 Personal Data is primarily stored and processed on servers located in India. In some cases, We may transfer or store Personal Data on servers, or share it with Data Processors, located in jurisdictions outside India.

9.2 The Company will not transfer Personal Data to any country or territory that has been restricted by the Central Government of India by notification. Where transfers are made, We rely on appropriate contractual and technical safeguards to protect Your Personal Data.

10. Data Retention

10.1 We retain Your Personal Data only for as long as is necessary for the purposes set out in this Policy, including for the time required to (a) provide the Services; (b) maintain business records; (c) comply with legal, accounting, tax and reporting obligations; (d) resolve disputes; and (e) enforce Our agreements.

10.2 Where Personal Data is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, and retention is not required under Applicable Law, We will erase such Personal Data or anonymise it.

10.3 We shall retain information (including user registration information) for at least 180 (one hundred and eighty) days after deletion or cancellation of Your Account, or such longer period as may be required by Applicable Law.

10.4 Documents You upload. Study documents You upload (textbooks, notes, question papers and similar files) are stored privately to Your account and are never shared with, or made accessible to, any other user. We retain them for as long as Your subscription is active, and delete them together with all text and images We extracted from them 60 (sixty) days after Your subscription ends. Where You do not hold a subscription, each uploaded document and everything extracted from it is deleted 60 (sixty) days after upload. Deleting Your account deletes them immediately. This paragraph is subject to Clause 10.7, which applies only to documents that have been declared as a licensed source for published material.

10.5 Scanned answer sheets. Where You upload photographs or scans of a handwritten answer sheet so that We can transcribe and grade it, the scan is stored privately to Your account and is never shared with, or made accessible to, any other user. We retain the scan for 60 (sixty) days from upload so that it remains available if You dispute the transcription or the marks awarded, and delete it automatically once that period ends. The transcribed text and Your result are kept with Your account as part of Your study record. Deleting Your account deletes the scan immediately.

10.6 Support attachments. Files You attach to a support report (typically screenshots) are used only to diagnose the issue You reported. We delete them as soon as the corresponding support ticket is resolved or declined, and in any event no later than 60 (sixty) days after You submit the report. Deleting Your account deletes them immediately.

10.7 Declared licensed source documents. Where a document is attached to material that is published or offered for sale on the Platform and is accompanied by a declaration of the licence under which it may be used, We retain that document, its declaration and the record of who made the declaration and when for as long as the published material remains available, and thereafter for as long as a claim in respect of it may be brought. This is a limited exception to Clauses 10.3 and 10.4: such a document is not deleted on the expiry of a subscription and is not deleted when the account that uploaded it is deleted. The reason is that the declaration is evidence of the basis on which third-party material was used, and a record that can be erased by the party who made it is not evidence on the day someone asks about it. This applies only to documents deliberately declared as a licensed source for published material; ordinary study documents You upload for Your own use are governed by Clause 10.4 and are deleted as described there.

11. Your Rights as a Data Principal

You have the following rights with respect to Your Personal Data:

  • Right to access information about Personal Data: You may obtain a summary of the Personal Data being processed by Us, the processing activities undertaken and the identities of the Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors with whom Your Personal Data has been shared.
  • Right to correction and erasure: You may request correction of inaccurate or misleading Personal Data, completion of incomplete Personal Data, updating of Personal Data and erasure of Personal Data that is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was processed, unless retention is required under Applicable Law.
  • Right of grievance redressal: You may file a grievance with the Company through the contact details in Clause 18 below. We will respond within a reasonable time and in any event within the timelines prescribed under Applicable Law.
  • Right to withdraw consent (as described in Clause 7 above).

To exercise any of these rights, please contact Our Officer at the address in Clause 18. We may require You to verify Your identity before acting on a request, and may decline requests that are manifestly unfounded, excessive, or prohibited under Applicable Law.

12. Children's Data and Special Categories

12.1 The Services are made available to Children only with the verifiable consent of a parent or lawful guardian. Where We become aware that a User is a Child, We will: (a) obtain verifiable parental consent before processing Personal Data; (b) refrain from processing Personal Data in any manner that is likely to cause any detrimental effect on the well-being of the Child; and (c) refrain from tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at Children.

12.2 A parent or guardian may, at any time, withdraw consent and request the erasure of the Child's Personal Data by writing to the Officer at the contact details in Clause 18.

12.3 The provisions of this Clause 12 shall, mutatis mutandis, apply to Personal Data of persons with disability whose lawful guardian acts on their behalf.

13. Cookies and Similar Technologies

13.1 We use cookies, pixels, beacons, software development kits (SDKs) and similar tracking technologies to deliver the Services, remember Your preferences, analyse usage, secure the Platform and personalise content. Categories include:

  • Strictly necessary cookies required for the Platform to function.
  • Functional cookies that remember Your settings, language and preferences.
  • Performance and analytics cookies (e.g., Google Analytics) that help Us understand how Users interact with the Services.
  • Advertising and marketing cookies set by Us or Our advertising partners, used only where permitted by law.

13.2 You can manage cookies through Your browser or device settings. Disabling certain cookies may impact the functionality of the Services.

14. Security Safeguards

14.1 We are concerned about safeguarding the confidentiality of your Information. We provide physical, electronic, and procedural safeguards to protect Information we process and maintain. For example, we limit access to this Information to authorized employees only who need to know that information in order to operate, develop or improve our Application/Services/products/Website. Please be aware that, although we endeavor to provide reasonable security for information we process and maintain, no security system can prevent all potential security breaches.

15. Personal Data Breach Notification

15.1 In the event of a Personal Data breach, the Company shall notify the Data Principal without undue delay, providing such particulars as are required by law.

16. Third-Party Services and Links

The Platform may contain links to third-party websites, applications and services, or integrate third-party tools (such as payment gateways, video conferencing platforms, analytics providers and learning-management partners). This Policy does not govern the privacy practices of such third parties. We encourage You to review their respective privacy policies before sharing any Personal Data.

17. Changes to this Policy

17.1 We may update this Policy from time to time to reflect changes in Our practices, Services or Applicable Law. The updated Policy will be posted on the Platform with a revised "Last Updated" date.

17.2 Where the changes are material, We will use reasonable efforts to notify You through the Platform, email, SMS or in-app notification. Your continued use of the Services after the effective date of the updated Policy constitutes Your acceptance of the changes.

18. Grievance Officer & Contact

The Company has appointed the following officer to address questions, exercise of rights and grievances relating to Personal Data:

Lokesh S Sharma
Email: support@cogniumlabs.io

19. Governing Law and Jurisdiction

This Policy shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India. The courts at Bangalore, Karnataka, shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any matter or dispute arising out of or in connection with this Policy, subject to the dispute-resolution mechanism set out in Our Terms of Service.
